# How viruses change

> *Viruses change faster than any other microbe. Error-prone copying, reshuffling of genome segments and recombination produce new variants within months.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Explain why RNA viruses mutate fast; distinguish antigenic drift from antigenic shift; relate change to vaccine updates and drug resistance |
| Mutation | Error-prone RNA polymerases; quasispecies; selection by immunity and drugs |
| Reassortment and recombination | Segmented genomes (influenza) and pandemics; diagram as a contrast of drift and shift |
| Consequences | Annual influenza vaccine updates; HIV drug resistance and combination therapy |
